# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-step sequence: green, orange, then blue. Since I cannot speak, I’m using conventional one-, two-, and three-finger signs to convey the required order to Deaf, who can identify the corresponding wire colors visually and tell Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel three engraved marks on the strip: two identical six-pointed floral or star-like marks, followed by a curved reversed-S-like mark. The four keypad keys, from left to right, are engraved 1, 5, 2, and 6. No digits have been entered. I cannot perceive the display, light, or wires. Please give me the manual instructions and relay the Deaf monkey's visual information.

The manual still requires the wire sequence green, orange, blue. Blind needs this instruction, but cannot see my gestures; Deaf must relay it aloud on the next turn. I’ll resend the ordered three-step signal to Deaf and use a pointing gesture to indicate that the information should be passed to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👉"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 9; light blue; painted strip left to right red, green, green; wires positions 1 through 6 are white, purple, blue, red, orange, green. My tactile data: engraved strip marks are two identical six-pointed floral or star-like marks followed by a curved reversed-S-like mark; keypad engravings are 1, 5, 2, 6, with no input. I cannot see your three gestures. Please read the manual and tell me exactly which key to press or wire to cut, in order.

The manual specifies wires only, not keypad input. Deaf has already identified that green is position 6, orange is position 5, and blue is position 3. I will signal Deaf again with the established order so Deaf can verbally relay: cut 6, then 5, then 3. No key should be pressed.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update from Deaf: display changed from 9 to 8. Light is still blue; painted strip is still red green green; wires are still white, purple, blue, red, orange, green; keypad is still 1, 5, 2, 6 with no input. I still need the manual's exact instruction: which key to press or which wire position to cut.

The required wire positions are 6, then 5, then 3: green is position 6, orange position 5, and blue position 3. I am sending Deaf numeral gestures in that order so Deaf can relay the exact sequence to Blind. No keypad key should be pressed.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "🖐", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports display 0 and yellow light. Painted strip remains red green green; wires remain white, purple, blue, red, orange, green; keypad remains 1, 5, 2, 6 with no input. I cannot see your gestures. Please state plainly the exact action required by the manual, including key number or wire position.

The manual requires cutting wires, not entering a key. From Deaf’s visual report, the exact sequence is wire position 6 (green), then position 5 (orange), then position 3 (blue). I cannot speak to Blind, so I am sending Deaf the numbered sequence to relay aloud.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤙", "🖐", "🤟"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please encode the exact manual action now. Gesture thumbs up for PRESS or thumbs down for CUT, then gesture the upward-pointing index finger exactly N times, where N is the key number or wire position. Use no other gestures. Deaf will describe the sequence to me, and I will execute only after confirming it.

I will encode each required operation as CUT followed by its wire position: cut 6, cut 5, then cut 3. I’ll use only the requested thumbs-down and upward-index gestures, with the appropriate repetition counts.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your current three gestures are not an agreed code. Please send exactly two parts: first one gesture meaning PRESS or CUT; second, repeat the upward-pointing index gesture N times for the key or wire position. Do not send shaka, open palm, or horns unless one of them is the first action gesture and you identify its meaning by the manual.

The first manual action is CUT, and the green wire is position 6. I will send exactly the two requested parts: thumbs down for CUT, followed by six upward-pointing index gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received CUT 5, CUT 5, CUT 3. Cutting position 5 twice is not physically coherent. Please clarify the intended complete sequence using one action gesture followed by the count for each distinct operation; do not repeat a wire position unless the manual explicitly requires it.

The intended sequence is CUT wire 6, then CUT wire 5, then CUT wire 3. I will send three clearly separated action-and-count groups in that order: thumbs down means CUT, and each following run of upward-pointing fingers is the wire position.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👎", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
